items.title: Liberal senator speaks out against Taylor's budget reply
items.description: Senator Andrew McLachlan raises concerns over Angus Taylor's use of the term "mass immigration" and plan to push tax-paying migrants off welfare benefits.

items.title: Live: Plibersek denies tax on discretionary trusts amounts to 'death tax'
items.description: Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek has denied that the government's tax on discretionary trusts amounts to a "death tax". Follow live.

items.title: 'Boomer bashing': Are cuts to private health rebates addressing generational or wealth inequality?
items.description: The federal government plans to reduce private health insurance rebates for older Australians, a move one advocate fears could "tip many over the edge".

items.title: Iran weekly briefing: New front emerges as UAE strikes back
items.description: The UAE shifts from target to combatant amid reports the US and Israel are preparing to renew strikes on Iran, writes Matthew Doran.

items.title: Fragile ceasefire holds, but fallout of Iran war is reshaping millions of lives
items.description: It has been more than two months since the US and Israel launched strikes in Iran. But the impact of the conflict continues globally.

items.title: Live: No Walsh for Queensland as Blues coach accidentally lists former Maroon
items.description: Billy Slater leaves Reece Walsh out of his Queensland side for State of Origin I, while NSW coach Laurie Daley accidentally announces the name of a former Maroon in his squad. Follow live.

items.title: Why the US, UK and NZ haven't raised interest rates in years
items.description: As Australians pay more on their mortgages, some countries have had no rise in their interest rate in recent years. So what's going on?

items.title: Tax is a great motivator but will Labor's changes fix Australia's housing mess?
items.description: The Albanese government and the opposition both want to turn back the clock on the Australian tax system.

items.title: The $10b offer Dave Hughes would 'hand on heart' turn down
items.description: Comedian Dave Hughes spoke to The Assembly about why he quit alcohol at 22, being "addicted to work" and the type of dad he's trying to be for his three kids.

items.title: Push for Australia to extract helium as Iran war impacts global supply
items.description: Helium is needed in health care and to make microchips and semiconductors, but the Middle East war has affected supply. Some think it is an opportunity for Australia's gas industry.

items.title: Live: ASX set to fall after Wall Street losses, AUD also lower
items.description: Australian markets are set to begin the week in negative territory, with ASX 200 futures pointing to a drop of around 0.4 per cent on Monday after both US indexes suffered losses after touching record highs. Follow live.

items.title: Homes destroyed, living in rubble, Gazans worry about dead awaiting burial
items.description: The families of Palestinians believed to be trapped under the rubble of collapsed buildings want to bury their dead.

items.title: 'Make it legal next time': Another blistering 100m for Aussie Nketia
items.description: For the second time this year, Eddie Nketia stops the clock in what would be an Australian record for the 100m, but is aided by an illegal tailwind.

items.title: Qld developer donation overhaul yields $170,000 in cash
items.description: More than $170,000 in donations from developers has been given to Queensland state politicians since laws banning developer donations were overturned in March.

items.title: How an Australian designer's fashion fame spurred a mental health unravelling
items.description: Rochelle Gregory has clothed everyone from Paris Hilton to Dua Lipa. Now the designer is using film to candidly explore her mental health battle while showcasing her latest collection.

items.title: Reasons it's so hard to end a long-term relationship, even when you want to
items.description: It's not just practical and emotional reasons that get in the way of executing a break-up. There are many ways your brain is making you want to stay.

items.title: Quiz: It's history time! Where was Pac-Man first released?
items.description: In what year did John Howard become a federal MP? And which country got to play Pac-Man first? Test yourself in this week's history quiz.

items.title: Mass showers and squalor: What spurred ex-Labor minister's NDIS fight
items.description: A former NSW Labor powerbroker and state disability minister pivotal in advocating for the establishment of the NDIS has warned against rushing through sweeping changes to the scheme.

items.title: Man found dead after fire at block of units in Ballarat's Wendouree
items.description: The man was pulled from the house by emergency crews, but could not be revived.

items.title: Criminal cases at risk of being halted as NT legal aid crisis worsens
items.description: Lawyers in the Northern Territory are commencing a landmark legal challenge that could require courts to halt some cases due to defendants being unable to access a lawyer amid a worsening legal aid crisis.

items.title: Advocates say more women being coerced and threatened to leave Australia
items.description: Advocates for migrant women say they're seeing more cases of exit trafficking — where an offender uses coercion, threats or deception to organise a person's departure from Australia.

items.title: Ukraine launches massive drone wave against Russia, killing four
items.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attacks were justified as "responses to Russia's prolongation of the war and its attacks on our cities and communities", two days after Russian strikes on Kyiv killed 24.

items.title: UAE slams 'dangerous escalation' after drone hits near nuclear plant
items.description: Abu Dhabi officials say radiation levels are normal and there was no damage to the plant, but authorities are now working to determine who carried out the attack.

items.title: Melbourne nightclub has operated for two years without insurance
items.description: Pride of our Footscray stopped paying public liability insurance when 18 insurers refused to underwrite the venue. The manager says operating without cover keeps staff on tenterhooks.

items.title: French Epstein probe sees 10 new alleged victims come forward
items.description: About 10 new suspected victims have come forward as part of a French probe into the network of late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
